claim_boundary: Measurement only; this receipt does not enforce ripr+ zero.
unresolved is the canonical_actionable_gap count from RIPR repo-badge-json: unsuppressed exposure gaps plus actionable test-efficiency findings.
active_unresolved equals unresolved; suppressed_unresolved is suppressed_exposure_gaps + suppressed_test_efficiency_findings from repo-badge-json.
top_files, top_gap_kinds, and recommended_first_clusters are triage aids derived from the seam inventory (repo-seams-json), not the headline count.
new_unresolved is null until PR diff comparison is wired in the quality gate.

reasons.reason: Generated status docs are verified through status-generation checks, not Rust test oracle exposure.
Archived source is retained for historical reference and is excluded from active workspace proof targets; current behavior must be proven in live crates instead.
Editor UX receipt tests are proof inputs validated by cargo/UX gates and fixture inventory; diff-scoped RIPR should not block on oracle gaps inside newly added receipt tests.

Issue #1567 adds inline_completion_ux_fixtures.rs as an executable completion-pack contract receipt for Try::Tiny positive, no-import, comment, string, POD, near-match, parse-damage, visible-symbol conflict, and stable-range cases. RIPR 0.9.x classifies the new fixture matrix and helper plumbing as production exposure even though the product seam is exercised through InlineCompletionProvider and the focused fixture test cargo test -p perl-lsp-rs-core --test inline_completion_ux_fixtures. Keep this suppression narrow to the single receipt file and remove when RIPR stops counting test fixture plumbing as production seams.

Issue #1962 centralizes perldoc URI and simple POD module-link parsing in PerlDocumentationTarget. Focused tests cover the accepted trimmed URI branch, whitespace rejection, alphanumeric/underscore tail acceptance, malformed target rejection, and the virtual-content current-module discriminator through from_perldoc_uri_accepts_already_trimmed_name_boundary, from_perldoc_uri_rejects_whitespace_instead_of_normalizing, perl_doc_name_segment_accepts_alphanumeric_and_underscore_tail, from_simple_pod_link_target_* tests, collect_simple_pod_module_links_boundary_discriminator, and parser_workspace_pod_related_perldoc_links_are_sorted_and_filtered. RIPR 0.9.x still reports weakly_exposed/infection_unknown seams for these string predicates and moved helper boundaries because the static tracer cannot connect the focused tests to the centralized resolver. Remove when EffortlessMetrics/ripr#1429 is fixed or targeted mutation replaces this advisory path.

Issue #1550 keeps the AC12 cancellation latency contract in aggregate average/p95/p99/p99.9 assertions while removing a per-sample 500us wall-clock assertion that can fail under scheduler preemption. RIPR 0.9.0 treats that test-receipt assertion change as weakly_exposed production risk even though the surface is an integration performance receipt and the contract remains covered by test_cancellation_check_latency_performance_ac12.

PR #3455 adds type hierarchy cancellation dispatch for textDocument/prepareTypeHierarchy, typeHierarchy/prepare, typeHierarchy/supertypes, and typeHierarchy/subtypes. Focused tests cover method registration (type_hierarchy_methods_are_registered_for_cancellation), immediate cancellation short-circuit and marker cleanup (cancelled_type_hierarchy_routes_return_immediate_responses), uncancelled live-handler dispatch and response values (route_request_call_presence_observer), and protocol-level cancellation behavior (lsp_cancellation_protocol_tests). RIPR 0.9.x still reports weak/static call-presence gaps on the method-string route helper and inline observer helper plumbing because it cannot trace the method matrix and RoutedResponse assertions through the dispatch helper. Remove when RIPR can trace routed string-dispatch call presence or targeted mutation replaces this static advisory path.

Seam-proof test files (ripr_seam_proof_*.rs) are diff-scoped proof harnesses whose internal plumbing — Ok(()) returns, .contains() calls, ? operators — must not be treated as new production seams by diff-scoped RIPR analysis. This is the same class as ripr-suppress-ux-receipt-tests. Tracks EffortlessMetrics/ripr#1428; remove when fixed upstream.

PR #4056 adds a fallible YAML contract test whose six diff-scoped RIPR gaps are test-harness plumbing (mapping/sequence parsing, Result propagation, exact contract values, and the terminal Ok(()) marker), not production behavior. The test directly observes the workflow's static runner, routing, fallback, trigger, permission, action-pin, and command-presence contracts; the production workflow remains subject to the normal workflow-policy and exact-head checks. This is the ripr#1428 test-surface limitation already covered by the repository's seam-proof suppressions. Remove when RIPR can distinguish contract-test plumbing from production seams.

xtask/tests/goals_next_json_cli.rs (#3692 defect 1, PR #3701) is a single-scenario Result<()> integration test driving the compiled xtask binary end to end to prove `goals next --json` emits parseable JSON on stdout and exits 1 on any internal error, never an unstructured color_eyre stderr dump. All 6 flagged seams (lines 29, 37, 39, 40, 58) are test-harness plumbing — the assert_cmd .assert() chain, the anyhow::anyhow!(...) message-building closure inside .map_err() (only reachable if the test's own invariant regressed), the ? error-path after it, and the terminal Ok(()) test-passed marker — not production behavior. Same ripr#1428 class as ripr-suppress-seam-proof-tests (test-harness plumbing flagged as production seams). The production seam this test proves (next()'s json=true branch in xtask/src/tasks/goals/mod.rs) is real and covered; only the test file's own scaffolding is suppressed. Remove when ripr#1428 is fixed upstream.

Canonical parse_quote_operator_content helper (centralized in #1289 refactor) has 4 ripr#1429-class seams: strip_prefix (A), chars.next (B), alphanumeric-guard predicate (C), checked_sub arithmetic (D). All seams are covered by inline seam-proof tests from PR #1292 (parse_quote_operator_content_wrong_operator_returns_none, _alphanumeric_delimiter_rejected, _underscore_delimiter_rejected, _mismatched_close_returns_none, etc.). RIPR cannot statically trace activation from string literals through the string-parsing call chain — same ripr#1429 limitation as removed per-consumer suppressions. Net reduction: 3 suppressions removed, 1 canonical suppression added. Remove when ripr#1429 is fixed upstream.

Test helper functions (extract_explicit_symbols in require_import_resolution.rs:304 and workspace_explicit_symbols_for_module in use_lib_fact_tests.rs:477) are diff-scoped RIPR false-positives in newly added integration test files. RIPR flags the match-arm / error-path plumbing in these helpers as production seams. The production behavior exercised by these helpers is fully covered by the conformance matrix tests in the same files. This is the same ripr#1428 class as ripr-suppress-seam-proof-tests (test-harness plumbing flagged as production seams). Suppression is minimal (two specific test files). Remove when ripr#1428 is fixed upstream.

is_word_boundary_before and is_word_boundary_after are char-aware word-boundary predicate helpers extracted for Codecov --lib coverage in PR #1288 (fix #956). Both predicates are covered by 4 inline #[cfg(test)] unit tests each (test_is_word_boundary_before_ascii, test_is_word_boundary_before_unicode, test_is_word_boundary_after_ascii, test_is_word_boundary_after_unicode). ripr 0.5.0 cannot statically trace activation from test inputs through the helper call chain — same ripr#1429 limitation as sibling suppressions. Remove when ripr#1429 is fixed upstream.

phase_block_description match arms (BEGIN/END/INIT/CHECK/UNITCHECK/wildcard) are ripr#1429-class no_static_path seams: RIPR cannot trace activation from string-literal call sites through the str match dispatch. All arms are covered by dedicated unit tests in hover_tests.rs with exact (strong-oracle) string assertions. Suppression is minimal (single production file, only hover_cards.rs). Remove when ripr#1429 is fixed upstream.

PR #1551 adds a live compiler hover guard that preserves the richer legacy Moo/Moose accessor hover card when compiler facts would return only a generic generated-symbol card. Direct unit tests cover both preserve and use-compiler branches, and moose_hover_completion_and_definition_include_attribute_metadata covers the e2e regression. RIPR cannot statically trace the feature-gated workspace_index.with_semantic_queries_for_uri -> hover_cutover -> should_preserve_legacy_hover propagation path, so this is a ripr#1429-class static tracing limitation. Suppression is narrow: single production file, issue #1550. Remove when ripr#1429 is fixed upstream or targeted mutation is scheduled.

Two boundary predicates in find_phase_block_at_offset (hover.rs:944 offset-range guard, hover.rs:953 phase_span boundary) are classified weakly_exposed despite ripr's own discriminate field reporting 'Strong oracle found: exact value or pattern assertion'. RIPR cannot statically trace propagation from the predicate branch through the recursive call chain to the test assertion. All four code paths are covered by exact-equality unit tests in hover_tests.rs. Suppression is minimal (single production file, only hover.rs). Remove when ripr#1429 is fixed upstream.

Seven ripr#1429-class seams in is_method_call_context and resolve_method_in_workspace (PR #1301 Slice 1): (A) 3 weakly_gripped paren-scan predicates — RIPR cannot trace coverage from char-literal unit tests through the iterative scan loop to predicate exits; (B) 2 equality-boundary seams (depth==1 and sym.name==method_name) with missing discriminators — same activation-tracing limit; (C) 4 activation_unknown seams in the cfg(feature='workspace')-gated resolve_method_in_workspace body — RIPR cannot statically traverse the feature guard and IndexAccessMode trait dispatch. All paths are covered: 6 unit tests for is_method_call_context (exact bool assertions), 2 lib-level None-path tests for resolve_method_in_workspace, and 3 integration tests for the full workspace-resolution path. Suppression is narrow (single production file, one PR). Remove when ripr#1429 is fixed upstream or targeted mutation is scheduled post-review.

Two ripr#1429-class files from PR #1302 Slice 2 (OO method inlay hints). impl_inlay_hints.rs: the new NodeKind::MethodCall arm in parameter_hints_with_resolver — RIPR cannot trace the dyn Fn resolver dispatch, walk_ast visitor callback chain, or predicate branch propagation (if-let chains, is_empty(), len()<=1, pos_in_range). All 6 branch paths are covered by inline #[cfg(test)] lib tests in impl_inlay_hints::tests plus 15 integration tests in inlay_hints_user_subs_unit.rs. misc.rs: the ws_resolver closure is gated on #[cfg(feature='workspace')], dispatches through LspServer trait, and contains JSON ? chains — same class as ripr-suppress-oo-method-signature-help-seams (PR #1301). Coverage: 6 inline lib tests exercise the resolver protocol; integration tests cover the mock-resolver path. Suppression is minimal: exactly two production files, one PR. Remove when ripr#1429 is fixed upstream.

Five ripr#1429-class seams in PR #1326 cfg(test)-strip helpers: cfg_test_line_numbers, structural_brace_delta, is_cfg_test_attr, strip_cfg_test_lines, resolve_source_path. RIPR cannot statically trace activation from string-literal test inputs through the line-by-line scanning loops to internal predicate branches (same class as parse_quote_operator_content and is_method_call_context). All seams are covered by 10 inline #[cfg(test)] unit tests: 3 for cfg_test_line_numbers (inline_test_module, empty_file, multiple_blocks), 3 for strip_cfg_test_lines (removes_test_block_lines, does_not_affect_production_hit_count, patch_coverage_full_for_test_only_pr), and 4 for structural_brace_delta edge cases added by the deep-review correctness fix. Retirement tracked in #1289. Remove when ripr#1429 is fixed upstream or when targeted mutation is scheduled.

Two ripr#1429-class seams in PR #1206 URI helpers: file_path_uri and windows_file_path_uri are Option<Uri>-chain helpers whose internal ? guards (Url::from_file_path().ok()?, chars().next()?, separator check, Url::parse().ok()?) cannot be traced by ripr from string-literal test inputs. All predicate branches are covered by 8 inline #[cfg(test)] unit tests covering both None-return guards and happy paths (Windows backslash, Windows forward-slash, Unix absolute path). Same ripr#1429 class as parse_quote_operator_content and is_method_call_context. Suppression is narrow (single production file). Remove when ripr#1429 is fixed upstream or targeted mutation is scheduled per #1289.

semantic_tokens_document_not_open is a ripr#1429-class seam in PR #1206: RIPR cannot statically trace activation from the inline #[cfg(test)] unit test (semantic_tokens_closed_document_error_includes_sync_guidance) through server.handle_semantic_tokens → get_document → ok_or_else closure → semantic_tokens_document_not_open. Same propagation-path limitation as find_phase_block_at_offset (hover.rs). The function is covered by a dedicated unit test with 5 exact message-content assertions. Suppression is narrow (single production file). Remove when ripr#1429 is fixed upstream or targeted mutation is scheduled per #1289.

ripr#1429-class seams across three debug_adapter files: (A) execution.rs weakly_gripped seams in all 6 resume handlers — lock_or_recover and stack_frames.clear(); RIPR cannot trace Mutex Some at compile time. (B) frames.rs reachable_unrevealed seam — Vec::new() degraded-transport fallthrough (line 73); reachable but RIPR cannot statically confirm coverage. (C) mod.rs reachable_unrevealed seams from four new #[cfg(test)] test-helper methods (seed_session_for_test, spawn_noop_child_for_test, inject_stack_frames_for_test, stack_frames_snapshot_for_test); ripr#1428-class false-positives (diff-scoped analysis treats #[cfg(test)] methods in production impl block as new production seams). All seams are covered by 5 unit tests (test_handle_continue/next/step_in/step_out/pause_clears_stack_frames) and 1 degraded-path integration test. Remove when ripr#1429 and ripr#1428 are fixed upstream.

Four ripr#1428-class false-positives in PR #901 hazard_invariant_tests helper functions (variables_body_is_empty and variables_success in the #[cfg(test)] mod): lines 584/591/607 are call_presence/weakly_gripped seams — handle_request call sites inside test helpers; line 597 is activation_unknown (vars == 0 boundary). These are pure test infrastructure, not production seams. The production invalid-ref guard (variables_ref_raw <= 0 || > i32::MAX, stale-ref DebugState::Stopped check) is covered by 9 integration tests in dap_variable_reference_hardening_tests.rs and 8 inline lib tests via hazard_invariant_tests. Same ripr#1428 class as ripr-suppress-quote-operator-conformance-test-helpers and ripr-suppress-seam-proof-tests. Remove when ripr#1428 is fixed upstream.

PR #3277 (epic #3276, PR1) removes the shipped --bridge flag so the perl-dap CLI is native-only. The change reshapes the clap-derived Args struct in crates/perl-dap/src/main.rs; ripr 0.9.x reports a no_static_path seam on the derive because it cannot trace activation through the clap #[derive(Parser)] proc-macro to a static test path. perl-dap/src/main.rs is a bin entry point (excluded from lcov coverage in this same PR); its CLI surface is covered by in-process #[bin] tests that render clap help and parse args (cli_help_has_no_bridge_product_surface, cli_rejects_removed_bridge_flag) plus the resolve_socket_port transport tests. Same proc_macro_opaque ripr#1429 class as the native_product_surface and xtask CLI suppressions. Suppression is narrow (single bin entry file, one PR #3277). Remove when ripr#1429 is fixed upstream or targeted mutation is scheduled per #1289.

ripr#1429-class equality-guard seams in collect_subroutine_declarations (name_str == sub_name, method_name == sub_name) and collect_package_declarations (name == pkg_name): match-guard equality predicates whose activation RIPR 0.9.0 cannot statically confirm via call-graph tracing. Both sides of all three boundaries are covered by 5 inline lib tests: subroutine_decl_collect_subroutine_declarations_finds_subroutine, subroutine_decl_boundary_discriminator_rejects_different_sub_name, method_decl_boundary_discriminator_rejects_different_method_name, package_decl_collect_package_declarations_finds_package, class_decl_boundary_discriminator_rejects_different_class_name. Remove when ripr can trace equality guard activation.

Two ripr#1428-class false-positives in PR #1283 lsp_smoke_e2e.rs: lsp_smoke_e2e_code_action_envelope and lsp_smoke_e2e_inline_completion_envelope are new end-to-end tests for codeAction and inlineCompletion envelope coverage (#949). This is the same ripr#1428 class as ripr-suppress-ux-receipt-tests and ripr-suppress-quote-operator-conformance-test-helpers (test-harness plumbing falsely classified as production seams). Suppression is minimal (single test file, test-only additions to the existing lsp_smoke_e2e.rs harness). Remove when ripr#1428 is fixed upstream.

PR #991 adds two test surfaces that diff-scoped RIPR 0.9.0 misclassifies as new production seams. (A) transport.rs gains an in-crate #[cfg(test)] mod (SharedBuf writer, framed_request/framed_raw/first_frame_body helpers, 11 test_transport_* functions) that drive the crate-private pub(super) run_with_io loop directly over std::io::Cursor; the tests live in-crate because run_with_io is not public and an external tests/ file would need a #[doc(hidden)] pub production shim. RIPR flags the test plumbing (struct/impl, predicates at line 252, return values) as production seams — same ripr#1428 class as ripr-suppress-dap-invalid-ref-hardening-test-helpers (variables.rs #[cfg(test)] mod). The transport framing seam (ContentLengthFramer recovery, CRLF/LF separators, malformed header/body, EOF, multi-message, recovery-after-bad-frame) and the no-session lifecycle handlers are fully exercised by these tests.
